summary: This .htaccess file locks down a directory by preventing any scripts from running. It does this in two ways: first by telling the web server to stop treating certain file types as executable scripts, and second by explicitly denying all web access to those dangerous file types.

explanations.2: This line tells Apache to treat PHP, Perl, Python, and other script files as CGI scripts, which is a setup step needed before you can disable them in the next line.
explanations.6: The FilesMatch directive uses a regular expression pattern (the stuff in quotes) to match filenames ending in .asp, .aspx, .cgi, .php, .pl, or .py — basically all the common script file types you want to block.
explanations.7: This denies access to anyone (from all) trying to request those matched files, so even if someone uploads a malicious PHP file, the web server won't serve it to them.
